items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: the next were several sessions with your orchestra, basically for Spike Hughes... Spike Hughes’ composition

ctx.x: Anyway, your own band got to record in a much more favorable light in March, although the March one is sort of a strange date there, too. There are a lot of vocals, and this is before Teddy Wilson. This is with Nicholas Rodriguez on piano, but the band is pretty much intact otherwise. You have Chu Berry and Sid Catlett. Just to refresh your memory, there’s Swing It, Synthetic Love, Spike Hughes’ composition, Six Bell Stampede, and Love, You’re Not the One for Me. Those have Benny Carter vocals.
I was hoping that you wouldn’t bring that up.

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Spike was coming and he would like to use my band... I enjoyed what we did.

ctx.x: He was a friend of John Hammond's, and John had recommended to him, I believe, that he use my band. Either that, or he had asked John about my band. I don't know. But I know that John relayed to me the fact that Spike was coming and he would like to use my band, and I think he augmented it with Coleman Hawkins and Henry Red Allen, I believe, and Higginbotham -- and they were not regular members of my orchestra at the time.
And he -- you know, he's written in a very favorable way about you in one or two of his, I guess, the second of his two-volume auto-biography - I'm talking about Spike Hughes, now.
